import json
from datetime import date, datetime

# Question 1: construction began 2005-02-23 and took exactly 8 years.
start = date(2005, 2, 23)
X = start.year + 8  # year the tower was ready

# Question 2: age of Natalie in days, birth 2008-03-22, today 2015-10-19.
birth_n = date(2008, 3, 22)
today_n = date(2015, 10, 19)
Y = (today_n - birth_n).days

# Question 3: whole months from 2005-06-14 to 2005-12-14 (same-day-of-month rule).
b = date(2005, 6, 14)
t = date(2005, 12, 14)
M = (t.year - b.year) * 12 + (t.month - b.month) - (1 if t.day < b.day else 0)
Z = M

# Derived offsets.
Xp = X - 1992
Yp = Y - 2756
Zp = Z + 1873

# Question 4: the date string "X'-Y'-Z'" is read as day-month-year.
joe_str = f"{Xp}-{Yp}-{Zp}"
joe_dt = datetime.strptime(joe_str, "%d-%m-%Y").replace(hour=14, minute=46)

exams = {
    "Jenny": datetime(1925, 10, 16, 0, 0),   # 16 Oct 1925, missing time -> 00:00
    "Kyle": datetime(1872, 6, 23, 5, 57),    # 23 June 1872 05:57
    "Joe": joe_dt,                           # X'-Y'-Z' at 14:46
    "Emma": datetime(1944, 5, 19, 14, 33),   # 19 May 1944 14:33
    "Jason": datetime(1851, 8, 1, 0, 0),     # Aug 1851, missing day/time -> 1 Aug 00:00
}

order = sorted(exams.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)
names = [name for name, _ in order]
final_list = "[" + ", ".join(names) + "]"

result = {
    "final_answer": final_list,
    "evidence": {
        "X": X,
        "Y": Y,
        "Z": Z,
        "Xp": Xp,
        "Yp": Yp,
        "Zp": Zp,
        "joe_date_string": joe_str,
        "joe_datetime": joe_dt.isoformat(),
        "descending_datetimes": {name: dt.isoformat() for name, dt in order},
    },
}

print(json.dumps(result))
